definitions.explanation: An animal's innate behavioral pattern or instinct. Used in biology and nature contexts to describe characteristic behaviors of a species.
A deeply ingrained habit or behavioral tendency in a person, often one that is hard to change. Implies the behavior has become almost instinctive.

examples.japanese: {猫|ねこ}には{夜行性|やこうせい}の{習性|しゅうせい}がある。
{渡|わた}り{鳥|どり}の{習性|しゅうせい}を{研究|けんきゅう}している。
examples.english: I'm researching the behavioral habits of migratory birds.

examples.japanese: この{昆虫|こんちゅう}は{光|ひかり}に{集|あつ}まる{習性|しゅうせい}があり、{夏|なつ}の{夜|よる}に{街灯|がいとう}の{周|まわ}りに{大量|たいりょう}に{見|み}られる。
examples.english: This insect has an instinct to gather around light, and large numbers can be seen around streetlights on summer nights.

examples.japanese: {値段|ねだん}を{確認|かくにん}するのは{職業|しょくぎょう}の{習性|しゅうせい}だ。
examples.english: Checking prices is a professional habit of mine.

examples.japanese: {記者|きしゃ}の{習性|しゅうせい}で、つい{質問|しつもん}してしまう。
examples.english: Out of a reporter's ingrained habit, I can't help asking questions.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{習性|しゅうせい}は{簡単|かんたん}には{直|なお}らないもので、{引退|いんたい}しても{朝|あさ}{早|はや}く{目|め}が{覚|さ}めてしまう。
examples.english: Long-standing habits don't change easily — even after retirement, I still wake up early in the morning.

notes:
USAGE NOTE:
Sense 1 (animal instinct) is the primary meaning. When applied to people (sense 2), it emphasizes that the behavior is so deeply rooted it has become almost involuntary.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {習性|しゅうせい}がある (have a habit/instinct)
- {動物|どうぶつ}の{習性|しゅうせい} (animal behavior/instinct)
- {職業|しょくぎょう}の{習性|しゅうせい} (professional habit)
- {長年|ながねん}の{習性|しゅうせい} (long-standing habit)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {本能|ほんのう}: instinct (more fundamental, biological drive)
- {癖|くせ}: habit, quirk (everyday word for personal habits, often negative)
- {習慣|しゅうかん}: habit, custom (neutral, broader usage)
